notes: The recorder, driven. Everything about the recording stayed the same; what changed is the page you drive it from. The sound and format switches are on the page itself now, so changing your mind no longer costs a second tab and a reload. After you choose what to share there are three seconds to get back to what you are recording, and the recording tab says what it is doing in its own title and icon, so you can find it again among fifteen. While it runs, a meter beside each sound source shows whether sound is actually arriving - a muted microphone used to read exactly like a working one. Stopping no longer drops a file into Downloads: the recording waits on the page, where you send it to Drive or save it to this PC, under a name you can edit first. It is held on disk until you do one of those, the tab asks before it closes on an unsaved one, and the next time you open the recorder it is still there. A recording's link pastes into a sheet as “Watch Me”, where a screenshot's says “Click Me”. Whichever way you stop - the floating timer, the page, or Chrome's own sharing bar - the recorder tab comes to the front, because that is where the recording is waiting. Space starts and stops it. A small floating timer now shows the clock and a Stop button while you work somewhere else. It is a picture-in-picture window, so it stays above every other window and is never minimised into the taskbar, and nothing at all is added to the page you are recording. On a whole-screen recording it is in the video, which it says itself - move it to another screen, or press Hide.
